# Data Structures

#### Course: DSA with C++

## Data Structures

Let's first briefly understand data structures.

A data structure is a way of storing data in an organized manner so that it can be accessed efficiently. We can classify such structures into two types.

Fundamental Data Structures

We know about vectors, arrays, maps, sets, etc. They are built-in data structures in C++ provided by STL (Standard Template Library).

Such data structures are called fundamental data structures.

Each of these data structures operates uniquely, and our choice among them depends on our specific requirements.

For instance, if we need to work with key-value pairs, it's better to use maps, even though we can perform the same task using a vector of pairs.

Custom Data Structures

Built-in data structures are not enough for writing complex programs.

Imagine working on a mapping service like Google Maps.

If we rely solely on built-in data structures to create a mapping service, our program won't be efficient.

In such cases, we employ logic to develop custom data structures such as graphs, trees, etc.

![Idea Emoji](data:image/png;base64,)

This course will cover all the major data structures, including various types of linked lists, heap, trees, and graphs.
